title: Greta's Smart Splash
markdown:
The sun blasted through Greta Holm's window. BAM! It was a bright, bold morning. Colors burst everywhere. Birds chirped a speedy, nonstop song. Greta stretched. Her muscles buzzed with the day's big possibilities. She could almost taste the fresh morning air. It smelled zesty, like grass wet with dew. Far away, warm toast tickled her nose. This was no normal Tuesday. This felt… HUGE. A day for big moves. A day to push limits.

Greta zipped to the kitchen. Her bare feet tapped a quick rhythm on the cool tiles. Her dad flipped golden pancakes. His moves were practiced, strong. "Morning, Greta! Big plans?" he boomed. His voice was warm, like the kitchen.

"Something’s cooking, Dad!" Greta grinned. She grabbed a mug. She'd heard the buzz all week. Excited whispers about a new town pool. A spectacular water place! Big, bold, splashy plans! The town felt awake. Shaking off sleepy cobwebs. Greta felt that spark too.

Later, Greta shoved her trusty blue towel into her bag. The air outside buzzed with activity. The town square was a whirl. Men in sharp suits rushed around. Their briefcases clicked on the pavement. A giant banner flapped like a sail. It read: "Pike's Progress: The Future is Wet!" And there, right in the middle, stood Alderman Pike. He was a big man. His suit seemed to pulse with importance. His booming voice filled every space.

"My friends!" he announced. His voice echoed. "Today, we start the most amazing pool this town has EVER seen! Picture this: shiny tiles that sparkle like diamonds! Think of diving boards that touch the sky! Think… MODERN!" He swept his arm in a wide arc. He pointed to a giant blueprint. A huge, fancy drawing.

Greta, her sturdy boots tapping a determined beat, pushed through the crowd. She liked things straightforward. She knew what made a good swimming spot. She peeked at the drawings. Big, yes. Fancy, for sure. But… where was the deep part? Where were the simple, strong changing rooms for kids after a swim? It looked more like a fancy fountain than a place for serious swimming.

Alderman Pike, always watching for admiring faces, saw her. "A smart observer!" he boomed. His smile was wide. "Young lady, what do you think of this brilliant idea?" He seemed to buzz with excitement, waiting for praise.

Greta took a deep breath. The morning sun felt warm and good. A clear, smart thought popped into her head. "Alderman Pike," she began. Her voice was surprisingly strong and steady. It cut through the noise. "It's… big. Very big. But the pool looks too shallow for proper swimming. And those fancy fountains you mentioned? They'll splash everywhere! Will there be enough room to actually… swim, without getting drenched by decorations?" She tapped the drawing. "And these changing rooms look pretty, but not very practical for a quick swim after a busy day. They seem… fragile."

Silence fell. Alderman Pike's smile wavered. Then it tightened. "Shallow? Not practical?" he sputtered. His booming voice lost some power. "My dear, this is about beauty! About town pride! It's about showing everyone we’re a town that MOVES FORWARD! A town that welcomes the future!"

"But," Greta insisted. Her gaze stayed steady. It met his surprised eyes. "Moving forward means building things that *work* for people, right? Not just things that *look* good for a photo?" She pointed to a spot on the plan. Her finger landed with precision. "This spot is good for a deep end. And maybe some more strong benches, not just fancy statues that are just for show?"

Alderman Pike sputtered more. His face turned a strange, alarming shade of red. The townspeople murmured. A quiet agreement spread. They saw Greta’s point. The shiny, grand plan suddenly seemed a bit… weak. More style than substance.

"Well," Pike huffed. He pulled at his perfect tie. "We shall… think about your… comments." He gave Greta a look. It wasn’t angry. It was more confused. He was used to cheers, not practical questions about water depth!

Greta felt a thrilling rush. She had spoken up! She had pointed out what really mattered. Not just for her, but for every swimmer in town. The pool would still be built. A symbol of the town's big dreams. But maybe, just maybe, it would be a pool for swimmers. Not just for show and fancy speeches.

She grabbed her towel. A huge, happy grin spread across her face. The sun felt even brighter. It was a spotlight on her brave words. "Today," Greta declared to the busy morning air. Her voice sparkled with new confidence. "Is going to be AMAZING!" She could already feel the cool water. It was calling her name. Ready for her powerful, fast kicks. The adventure was just beginning. And Greta Holm was ready. Every splash. Every wave.
characters: Greta Holm the municipal swimmer, Alderman Pike the civic moderniser
